authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: Platts p. 530 s.v. do/du expressly gives do-pahar noon (Sanskrit dvi-prahara). The Hindi Rohili survey records dupahar (kannauji p. 84). These whole do-/du-pahar responses are linked to the existing Hindi word as a provisional regional route; the actual immediate Indo-Aryan transmitter remains uncertain. The donor already has an older graph link to *dva-prahara; that reconstruction differs from Platts’s dvi-prahara and is flagged in noon-upstream-audit.json, not silently treated as verified. Exact survey form doper is retained.
